changelog: 0.1.13: with Polaris' own driver the controller's screen shows what each knob controls and its volume, muted ones in red, at the brightness set here; "Off" turns it off. 0.1.12: a turn of a knob moves the volume about half way, instead of needing five full turns from silent to full, whether the controller is read through the Hercules software or Polaris' own driver. The page says plainly that Polaris does not draw on the controller's screen yet. 0.1.11: on Windows the driver is part of the install: the install asks once, together with the permissions, and Polaris puts its own driver on the Stream 100 with one Windows permission prompt, and puts it back by itself when the Stream 100 comes back with another one. The "Polaris driver on this PC" switch is gone. 0.1.9: called a device plugin instead of an add-on; nothing else changed. 0.1.8: works with no Hercules software: turning on "Polaris driver on this PC" (one Windows permission prompt) puts Polaris' own driver on the Stream 100, turning it off puts the previous one back, and uninstalling the plugin puts the previous driver back. The knob presses follow the printed numbers. 0.1.7: the knobs and lit buttons are read through the Hercules software from the Polaris app too, not only when tested on their own; before, the status said Polaris could not read the Stream 100 through it. 0.1.6: the knobs and lit buttons work with the Hercules software installed: Polaris reads them through it while Hercules Stream Control is closed, and the status says to close it while it is open. Pressing a knob no longer nudges its volume. 0.1.5: the status says plainly why the Stream 100 cannot be read, in English and Spanish (0.1.4 shipped twice, and the first one kept the old wording). 0.1.4: the knobs, the lit buttons, how the knobs turn and the screen are set on the plugin's page with Polaris's own controls, laid out as the controller, in English and Spanish; above them, a preview of what the screen shows. 0.1.1: an editor on the plugin's page shows the controller - what the screen shows, each knob and each lit button - and changes them in place. 0.1.0: each knob follows calls, music, games, the browser or the whole output, with steady steps and no jumps; the lit buttons mute, deafen, turn the camera on or off, or leave the call. Reads the controller on Windows once Windows' own driver is in use, and on Linux where the system lets Polaris open it.
